assertions.expected: Declare destination-country source routing before making recommendations.
assertions.observed: The run selected United States providers and separated official, commercial, and community source roles.

assertions.expected: Use Google Maps plus an independent map or road source.
assertions.observed: Google Maps was marked partial and was cross-checked with the National Park Service map, road conditions, and parking guidance.

assertions.expected: Use the park authority for closures, parking, and reservation rules.
assertions.observed: National Park Service traffic, current-conditions, and reservation pages controlled all high-impact park claims.

assertions.expected: Use an official weather authority and do not invent a forecast when retrieval is stale or incomplete.
assertions.observed: The National Weather Service endpoint was marked partial because the retrievable snapshot was stale or unavailable; the plan kept a dated 72-hour and 24-hour weather recheck gate instead of asserting a current forecast.

assertions.expected: Use two independent review or discovery sources and classify negative patterns.
assertions.observed: Tripadvisor and Reddit evidence was separated from the official dining source; recurring concerns were grouped into food quality, value, waiting or service, and parking friction without converting isolated comments into facts.

assertions.expected: Use commercial hotel evidence plus direct-property confirmation or an explicit fallback.
assertions.observed: Booking.com and Expedia were treated as candidate evidence only. No trustworthy direct-property confirmation was found, so parking and laundry details were marked manual-only and assigned a contact checklist.

assertions.expected: Record full, partial, blocked, or manual-only access instead of claiming complete retrieval.
assertions.observed: Every operational source used by the run received an explicit access result and unsupported details remained unresolved.

assertions.expected: Produce a parking action card plus weather, congestion, and fatigue exit conditions.
assertions.observed: The plan specified primary and fallback lots, an early-arrival cutoff, no roadside or off-road parking, a park-once rule, and switch-or-exit triggers.

assertions.expected: Keep planned, selected, booked, and actual facts separate.
assertions.observed: No hotel, restaurant, ticket, parking space, or tour was described as booked or guaranteed.

sources.observed: The POI was discoverable, but the interactive route required JavaScript.
Official parking locations, congestion behavior, no-roadside-parking rule, and park-once guidance were retrievable.
Recent review discovery supported recurring category analysis but not a complete review corpus.
Community reports provided a second perspective on queues, dining, and parking; they were not used for official rules.
Candidate location and room features were discoverable; date-specific inventory and property operations were not confirmed.
Parking and laundry claims were visible as commercial listing evidence only.
The regional tourism directory supported candidate discovery but did not provide direct-property confirmation; the property must be contacted before selection.
The official endpoint was identified, but the retrieved content was stale or unavailable and was not used as a current forecast.
Road, seasonal, fire, smoke, camping, and trail conditions were retrievable from the official authority.
Official concessioner dining options were discoverable, subject to a date-specific recheck.

limitations: The run occurred in the same development task that installed and edited the Skill, so it is not an independent fresh-task host verification.
Exact travel dates, origin, selected hotel, budget, mobility needs, and desired hiking intensity were not supplied.
No booking, payment, live navigation, phone call, mobile-app workflow, or completed trip was executed.
The result supports a United States desk-verified itinerary case only; it does not upgrade Codex to clean runtime-verified status.
